title: The Illusion of What If: Evaluating the Breakdown of Counterfactual Reasoning in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.27953v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Counterfactual reasoning requires models to reason beyond the observed world and explain how altered conditions propagate through downstream consequences. Existing benchmarks largely target bounded settings with fixed variables or single gold outcomes, overlooking open-domain scenarios requiring causal-process evaluation. To this end, we present $\textbf{WhatIfBench}$, a diagnostic benchmark for open-domain, open-form, long-horizon counterfactual causal reasoning, containing 220 what-if questions across STEM, HSS, and Hybrid scenarios. To evaluate free-form responses, we further propose $\textbf{PRISM}$, which first converts each natural-language explanation into a Response-Derived Semantic Causal Graph of events, states, and mechanisms. translated_title: “假如”的幻觉：评估大语言模型反事实推理的失效
translated_abstract: 反事实推理要求模型超越观察到的世界进行推理，并解释改变的条件如何传播并影响下游后果。现有基准主要针对具有固定变量或单一标准答案的有界设置，忽略了需要因果过程评估的开放域场景。为此，我们提出了 WhatIfBench，一个针对开放域、开放形式、长程反事实因果推理的诊断性基准，包含涵盖 STEM（科学、技术、工程、数学）、HSS（人文社会科学）和混合场景的 220 个“假如”问题。为评估自由形式的回答，我们进一步提出了 PRISM，它首先将每个自然语言解释转换为包含事件、状态和机制的“响应衍生语义因果图”。在该图的基础上，PRISM 联合应用两项指标：过程指标（Process Metric）评估图级别的因果有效性，评分细则指标（Rubric Metric）评估答案层面的解释充分性。对六个前沿大语言模型的评估……
tldr: 该论文提出了 WhatIfBench 诊断基准（含 220 个跨学科“假如”问题）和 PRISM 评估框架（将自由回答转化为语义因果图进行过程与结果双重评估），揭示了大语言模型在开放域长程反事实因果推理中的系统性失效。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces WhatIfBench, a diagnostic benchmark of 220 what-if questions for open-domain, open-form, long-horizon counterfactual causal reasoning, along with PRISM, an evaluation framework that converts free-form responses into semantic causal graphs to jointly assess causal validity and explanatory adequacy, revealing systematic breakdowns in frontier LLMs' counterfactual reasoning.
